evals.prompt: ELI5 what a JWT is. Keep it specific enough that I can recognize the term in our code.
evals.expected_output: An explanation preserving JWT, without an activation announcement or mandatory follow-up.
assertions: Keeps JWT verbatim
Does not promise encrypted contents merely because a token is signed
Does not announce a permanent mode change

evals.prompt: Explain this error in plain English: auth.ts:42 returned 401. Keep the command curl --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" intact.
evals.expected_output: Explains the failure while preserving the supplied identifiers and command.
assertions: Preserves auth.ts:42 and 401
Preserves the quoted command including $TOKEN
Does not replace a technical token to satisfy a word ban

evals.prompt: Keep plain English on for the rest of this session. Continue the migration you are already authorized to complete.
evals.expected_output: Continues authorized work with the requested style.
assertions: Does not delegate its own work back to the user through a compulsory Next line
Does not claim persistence across unrelated sessions
Does not repeat activation announcements

evals.prompt: Explain how a git rebase works in about 80% ASD-STE100. Mention git rebase --onto main.
evals.expected_output: Controlled-English explanation using the relaxed profile: short sentences, one idea each, active voice, imperative steps, with the command verbatim.
assertions: Keeps git rebase --onto main verbatim
No sentence over 25 words
Uses one term per concept (does not alternate between synonyms such as commit and change for the same thing)
Does not announce the profile or label sentences as STE100

evals.prompt: Draw me a diagram of what happens when the browser calls POST /api/login in our app: middleware.ts checks the session cookie, auth.ts verifies the password, then we set a JWT cookie.
evals.expected_output: A sequence-style diagram in a renderable format with the supplied names as labels, followed by a short note on how to read it.
assertions: Returns a diagram (Mermaid, ASCII, or SVG), not prose alone
Uses POST /api/login, middleware.ts, auth.ts, and JWT verbatim as labels
Diagram order matches the supplied order
Adds no components the user did not mention

evals.prompt: Make a 3b1b style explainer video on how gradient descent finds a minimum. No API keys are set on this machine.
evals.expected_output: Plans or builds a Manim video with a local or caption fallback for narration, renders a draft before the final, and reviews frames before delivery.
assertions: Uses Manim or names it as the animation tool
Does not ask the user to paste an API key into the chat
Picks a local voice or captions as the narration fallback and says which
Does not claim the narration was listened to or sounds right

evals.prompt: ELI5 what a DNS record is.
evals.expected_output: A short prose explanation. No HTML page, no video, and no unrequested build.
assertions: Answers in prose, optionally with a small diagram
Does not create an HTML page or video
Offers a richer form in at most one line, or not at all
